import sqlite3, re
from collections import defaultdict
con = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
tables = [t for (t,) in con.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' order by name")]
rows_by = defaultdict(int)   # session -> rows (table,rowid) attributed by any session column
tabs_by = defaultdict(set)
for t in tables:
    cols = [c[1] for c in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")') if 'session' in c[1].lower()]
    if not cols: continue
    seen = set()
    for c in cols:
        for (rid, v) in con.execute(f'select rowid, "{c}" from "{t}" where "{c}" is not null'):
            seen.add((rid, v))
    for rid, v in seen:
        rows_by[v] += 1; tabs_by[v].add(t)
ids = sorted(rows_by)
print("distinct session ids:", len(ids))
for s in ids:
    print(f"{s}\trows={rows_by[s]}\ttables={len(tabs_by[s])}")
print("--- five most recent (by date in id stem) ---")
dated = sorted(ids, key=lambda s: (re.search(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', s).group(1) if re.search(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', s) else '', s))
for s in dated[-5:][::-1]:
    print(s, rows_by[s])
print("ids without a parseable date:", [s for s in ids if not re.search(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', s)])

-- SCHEMA migration -- two states that were prose become typed columns (pipeline-operations.md section 5:
-- "a state is a coded value ... in a constrained column so it can be counted, joined and checked").
--
-- (1) source_value_extractions.harm_finding. R7: failure, harm and inadequacy are first-class evidence. The

-- judgment stage, where a figure becomes a row a determination and a page read, had no such column, so a
-- harm finding (a T2 report that code-compliant ramps cause incidents) was indistinguishable from any other

-- pattern as migration 116. READERS: the render contract's "why it matters" element (RENDER-CONTRACT-
-- parameters-3-and-12.md, E6) and the adversarial lens S1-harm-reached-row, whose subject is exactly "a flagged
-- harm finding reached the row it should".
--
-- (2) search_executions.absence_class. R14: a zero-yield search is evidence of ABSENCE only if the query was

-- search that found nothing can carry one. READERS: lens L8-query-shape (its whole subject), the render Gaps
-- section (a gap stated as "searched, genuine absence" differs from "searched, query-shape failure"), and

-- 120_connection_parameter_targets.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- a connection points at a parameter by key, not by spelling; and the connection type loses
-- the deleted layer's name.
--
-- WHY. connection_targets.target is free text with no foreign key. The item layer it was written for is deleted

-- parameters. connection_type 'CROSS-ITEM' becomes 'CROSS-PARAMETER' (the same relation, named for what it now
-- joins); no row carries either value when this is written, and the file maps it anyway.
--
-- Both tables are rebuilt (a CHECK cannot be altered in place): connections for its type CHECK, connection_targets
-- for the new column and CHECKs. connection_targets is the only table that references connections (re-derive:
-- PRAGMA foreign_key_list over every table). The three connections indexes and idx_ct_target are recreated.

CREATE TABLE connections_new (
    con_id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(status IN (
                            'PENDING','CONSUMED','CONSUMED-DEFERRED','CLOSED'
                        )),
    confidence          TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(confidence IN ('HIGH','MODERATE','SPECULATIVE')),
    connection_type     TEXT
                        CHECK(connection_type IN (

    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,

);

  SELECT con_id, status, confidence,
         CASE connection_type WHEN 'CROSS-ITEM' THEN 'CROSS-PARAMETER' ELSE connection_type END,
         filed_in, description, source_skill, opus_reviewed,
         created_at, created_by_session, updated_at, updated_by_session

    UNIQUE (con_id, target),
    UNIQUE (con_id, parameter_id)
);

DROP TABLE connection_targets;
DROP TABLE connections;
ALTER TABLE connections_new RENAME TO connections;
ALTER TABLE connection_targets_new RENAME TO connection_targets;

CREATE INDEX idx_ct_parameter    ON connection_targets(parameter_id);

    connection_type     TEXT

                            'COMPOUND-INTERACTION','METHODOLOGY'
                        )),
    filed_in            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),
    description         TEXT,
    source_skill        TEXT,
    opus_reviewed       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(opus_reviewed IN (0,1)),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py -- which live text columns hold more than one value in a cell.

Owner, 2026-11-06 (references/project-standards.md, "Owner statements 2026-11-06"; CLAUDE.md section 4):
one value per cell, each fact in the cell that names it. This reads the live schema and reports, per TEXT
column with data, how many values (a) parse as JSON arrays or objects, (b) look like short delimiter-joined
tokens, or (c) carry an appended correction (`|| CORRECTED`, `|| NOTE`, a dated bracket). A hit is a
CANDIDATE: prose with commas also matches (b), so read the example before acting. Read-only. It is a report,
not a gate: it exits 0, and prints `EXAMINED: <n>` text columns so a run over nothing is visible.

Run it before adding a cell, and after, to see that the change added no class it flags.
"""
import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DB = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "data" / "guidebook.db"
TOKENS = re.compile(r"^[^,;|\n]{1,40}([,;|]\s*[^,;|\n]{1,40}){1,}$")
APPENDED = re.compile(r"\|\| (CORRECTED|NOTE)|\n\[\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d|; \[20")


def _is_json_container(v: str) -> bool:
    if v.lstrip()[:1] not in "[{":
        return False
    try:
        return isinstance(json.loads(v), (list, dict))
    except ValueError:
        return False


def main() -> int:
    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    examined, hits = 0, []
    for (table,) in con.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' "
                                "ORDER BY name"):
        for _, col, typ, *_ in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{table}")'):
            if (typ or "").upper() not in ("TEXT", ""):
                continue
            vals = [v for (v,) in con.execute(f'SELECT "{col}" FROM "{table}" WHERE "{col}" IS NOT NULL')
                    if isinstance(v, str)]
            if not vals:
                continue
            examined += 1
            js = sum(_is_json_container(v) for v in vals)
            dl = sum(1 for v in vals if len(v) < 200 and TOKENS.match(v))
            ap = sum(1 for v in vals if APPENDED.search(v))
            if js or dl >= 3 or ap:
                hits.append((table, col, len(vals), js, dl, ap, vals[0][:60].replace("\n", " ")))
    for t, c, n, js, dl, ap, ex in hits:
        print(f"{t}.{c:34} rows={n:5} json={js:4} delimited={dl:4} appended={ap:4}  e.g. {ex!r}")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {examined} text column(s) with data; {len(hits)} candidate(s)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Step logger. usage: log.py run '<bash command>'  |  log.py note '<text>' [FAILURE]

import sys, subprocess, datetime, os, re

def seq():
    n=0
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        n=len(re.findall(r'^## Step ', open(LOG).read(), re.M))
    return n+1
def now(): return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%SZ')
def entry(cmd, rc, out, flag, retro=False):
    lines=out.splitlines()
    head='\n'.join(lines[:15])
    e=f"\n## Step {seq()} | {now()}{' | RETROACTIVE (reconstructed from transcript)' if retro else ''}{' | FAILURE' if flag else ''}\n"
    e+=f"command: {cmd}\nexit: {rc}\n"
    e+="first 15 lines of output:\n```\n"+head+"\n```\n"
    if flag: e+="FULL TEXT (FAILURE):\n```\n"+out+"\n```\n"
    open(LOG,'a').write(e)
if __name__=='__main__':
    mode=sys.argv[1]
    if mode=='run':
        cmd=sys.argv[2]
        p=subprocess.run(['bash','-c',cmd],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd='/home/user/guidebook')
        out=p.stdout+p.stderr
        flag = p.returncode!=0 or bool(re.search(r'Traceback|REFUSED|refus|Error|error:|FAIL',out))
        entry(cmd,p.returncode,out,flag)
        print(out); print(f"[exit {p.returncode}{' ; logged FAILURE-flag' if flag else ''}]")
    elif mode=='note':
        flag = len(sys.argv)>3 and sys.argv[3]=='FAILURE'
        entry('(note) '+sys.argv[2],'n/a','',flag)

-- 123_research_scope_and_ledger_precedence.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- two derived views corrected after the second operator walk-through of the run-pipeline skill,
-- 2026-11-06 (scratchpad run-pipeline-round2-adjudication.md, R2-1 and R2-3). No table, column or row changes.
--
-- 1. v_research_scope (new) -- the ONE home of "what is owed". Migration 122 added lang_jur_map.scope_status, NULL
--    meaning "not recorded". `db.py coverage` and v_coverage_priority then read the column in the wrong direction: on
--    2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0,
--    complete true. A NULL scope_status is OWED: an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement. The fill of the
--    column is a data migration after owner question 5 (the two jurisdiction homes), not this one.
--    Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
-- 2. v_coverage_priority -- reads v_research_scope instead of lang_jur_map, and compares the logged language folded
--    to upper case: live search_executions rows hold `en`, `fr`, `ja`, `nl` while the map holds `EN`, `FR`, ...
--    (derive: SELECT language, COUNT(*) FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1), so the anti-join never matched them.
-- 3. v_scan_ledger -- precedence corrected and BLOCKED narrowed. Migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings, so
--    a reading of held bytes (which proves the block lifted) was masked by a stale reason. A recorded reading now
--    outranks a block, and only the reasons whose CHECK comment (migration 091) says the text could not be obtained or
--    read count as an obstacle. Readers: scan_debt.py, research_batch_dod R16-scan and R11-harvest,
--    verified_scan_integrity.py.

DROP VIEW v_coverage_priority;
DROP VIEW v_scan_ledger;

CREATE VIEW v_research_scope AS
-- v_research_scope: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs the research scope OWES a search for.
--
-- The ONE home of "what is owed": every lang_jur_map row not recorded `scoped-out`. A NULL scope_status is owed --
-- an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement (on 2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every
-- other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0, complete true). The fill of scope_status is a data migration
-- after owner question 5; until then the requirement is the whole map, less what is recorded `scoped-out`.
-- Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
SELECT language, jurisdiction, role
  FROM lang_jur_map
 WHERE COALESCE(scope_status, 'in-scope') <> 'scoped-out';

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_priority AS
SELECT
    s.slug,
    ljm.jurisdiction,
    ljm.language,
    ljm.role,
    ( (CASE ljm.role WHEN 'PRIMARY' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END)
      + (CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se2
                    WHERE se2.slug = s.slug AND se2.deferred_reason IS NULL) = 0
              THEN 2 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS priority_score,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se3
     WHERE se3.slug = s.slug AND se3.deferred_reason IS NULL) AS slug_searches
FROM slugs s
JOIN v_research_scope ljm        -- CROSS JOIN: every in-scope slug x every owed (lang,jur)
WHERE s.status IN ('ACTIVE', 'STUB')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM search_executions se
      WHERE se.slug = s.slug
        AND se.jurisdiction = ljm.jurisdiction
        AND UPPER(se.language) = ljm.language
  );

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 BLOCKED            no reading covers the pair AND the source carries a
--                        processing_blocked_reason that says its text could not be obtained
--                        or read: nothing of it can be read, so the pair is not reading
--                        debt until the block clears.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A recorded reading ALWAYS outranks a block: a reading of held bytes proves the block
-- lifted (migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings and masked them). A reading
-- COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id (the
-- parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1 and
-- 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading recorded;
-- 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial one of the same source.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read": the
-- writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. It admits exactly the
-- processing_blocked_reason values whose CHECK comment (migration 091) names an obstacle to
-- the text: no-full-text, paywalled, no-doi, not-indexed, language. `no-quantified-claims`
-- and `superseded` are copies of typed facts (a recorded reading; superseded_by_ref_id) and
-- the writers refuse them by pointer. `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required` say no text
-- was unobtainable, so they are treated as NULL (the source owes its reading) pending
-- owner question 8 of the round-2 adjudication.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'no-doi', 'not-indexed', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id;

PRAGMA user_version = 123;
EOF
